overview: A Danish-Swedish sound town and castle site where Christopher of Bavaria died in 1448.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Helsingborg was a strategically vital Danish fortified town on the Sound, controlling the narrowest crossing between Scania and Zealand. Christopher of Bavaria died suddenly there in 1448 without an heir.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: Christopher's death at Helsingborg reopened the Scandinavian succession and led to the election of Christian I as the first Oldenburg king of Denmark. The town's position on the Sound made it economically and militarily significant throughout the conflict over Hanseatic and Danish maritime dominance.
